mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to expected future cash flows, lowering the present value of equities and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for at least 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in the identified regime, or the Fed rate reverts before the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a faster than expected tightening cycle, prompting a flight to quality and a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for at least 2 months
regime_hint: accelerating inflation in the core economy
failure_condition: Over 50 such inflation spikes fail to produce statistically significant positive 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05) in the subsequent 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) of more than 50,000 jobs in a single month coincides with increased consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, driving a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: In 30% of such labor spikes, the 5-day forward return is non-positive (≤ 0%) or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly GDPC1 personal consumption expenditure growth exceeds 4% for two consecutive quarters, it indicates robust demand that supports higher corporate earnings expectations and yields a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by more than 4% in two consecutive quarterly periods
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during 40% of such demand episodes in the walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of 5% or more signals supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 30 such contractions do not result in a statistically significant negative 60-day forward return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) above 1% monthly growth for three months indicates dual demand channels, leading to a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1% growth and RSAFS > 1% growth for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in 40% of such interaction periods.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for four consecutive months, it suggests a tightening labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and remains below for at least 4 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in 60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% for five consecutive months, in the absence of accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%), creates a risk-off environment that produces a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for five consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 2% over the same period
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05) in 70% of such low-rate-inflation regimes.
